views.reconstructed_statement: Let S={0,...,7} and define L:S->S by L(s)=(s XOR 3) mod 8, where 3 is the fixed three-bit mask 011. The root is the conjunction of: (1) for every s in S, L(L(s))=s; (2) in increasing input order 0,...,7, its eight outputs are exactly [3,2,1,0,7,6,5,4]; and (3) for every seven-bit assignment z:{0,...,6}->{0,1}, the program X on wire 0 followed chronologically by X on wire 1 produces a state z' whose little-endian address value z'(0)+2z'(1)+4z'(2) is ((z(0)+2z(1)+4z(2)) XOR 3) mod 8, and applying that same two-gate program twice returns the entire seven-bit assignment z. The third conjunct contains both the address equation AND equality of the full state after two applications. There are no assumptions about the address, row bits, or work bit: all 128 basis assignments are quantified over. By the supplied X action, one application changes bits 0 and 1 to their complements and preserves every other wire. This toggles the two low address bits and preserves address bit 2. The operation is bitwise XOR with the mask, not addition of three modulo eight: for example input 1 maps to 2.

views.reconstructed_statement: For any natural number q of wires and every well-formed finite reversible program p made of X, controlled-X on distinct wires, and doubly-controlled-X on pairwise distinct wires, write E(p) for its chronological basis permutation and P(E(p))[r,c]=1 when r=E(p)(c), and 0 otherwise. Its compiled primitive program has a bare circuit C_p and a stored exact real angle theta_p. The full evaluation is D_p=exp(i theta_p) C_p, with chronological circuit multiplication C(g::rest)=C(rest)C(g). The root asserts all five statements simultaneously: (1) universally over q,p, D_p=P(E(p)) as exact complex matrices; (2) the specific compiled seven-wire primitiveAccess3Program has the stored, unreduced angle theta_star=45*pi/8, where 45/8 is real division; (3) universally over q,p, C_p=exp(i theta_p)^(-1) P(E(p)); (4) exp(i theta_star) is not 1; and (5) the bare circuit of that specific seven-wire program is not equal as a matrix to P(e_star), where e_star is the separately named primitiveAccess3BasisEquiv. The named e_star is not unfolded in this packet. The specific source program applies X0,X1, then CCX(3,0;6),CCX(6,1;2),CCX(3,0;6),CCX(3,0;1),CX(3;0),CCX(4,1;2),CX(4;1),CX(5;2), in that order. It has five CCX gates. Each supplied CCX macro accumulates two H angle fields (total pi) and four T minus three Tdagger angle fields (net pi/8), hence stores 9*pi/8; X and CX store zero. The five copies therefore store 45*pi/8. As a complex scalar, exp(i theta_star)=exp(-3*pi*i/8), while its inverse is exp(3*pi*i/8). Thus the generic bare-circuit formula applied to the displayed source program gives a nontrivial scalar multiple of that program's ideal basis permutation. The last conjunct is an exact matrix inequality, and does not say that the phase-correct full compiler output is incorrect.

views.reconstructed_statement: Fix the one record p=warmRobinParameters with n=3,kappa=7,functionPieces=1,polynomialDegreeCost=1. From the supplied natural-valued formulas, clog2(3)=2, clog2(1)=0, clog2(7)=3, so its six register-group widths (mf,indicator,sparseIndex,odPureAncilla,system,ancilla) are (5,1,3,0,3,1), the total width is 13, and the basis dimension is D=2^13=8192. Its indicator-bit position is ancilla+system+odPureAncilla+sparseIndex=1+3+0+3=7. For every natural number j, define s(j)=(j shifted right by 1) AND 7, define b(j)=1 if 2<=s(j)<=5 and 0 otherwise, and define f(j)=j XOR (b(j) shifted left by 7). Thus f toggles bit 7 exactly when the three system bits 1,2,3 encode one of 2,3,4,5, and preserves every other bit. The root asserts the conjunction of four conclusions: (1) f(f(j))=j for EVERY natural j, with no j<D restriction; (2) the finite self-map F of {0,...,8191}, obtained by F(j)=f(j) with the supplied image-bound proof, is injective and surjective; (3) there exists an equivalence e of {0,1,2} for which e(e(x))=x fails for at least one x; and (4) the two separately named stored matrices U_indic_dagger(p).matrix and U_indic(p).matrix are equal. Both stored arrays are literally the same 8192-by-8192 function M(i,j), equal to the symbolic constructor Coeff.rat(1) when i=f(j), and Coeff.rat(0) otherwise. Their equality is therefore an equality of the supplied symbolic arrays by their definitions. Coeff is an inductively generated expression syntax, and no complex evaluation, matrix-multiplication law, actual conjugate transpose, or physical realization theorem is asserted by this equality. A witness illustrating the independent third conjunct is the cycle e(x)=x+1 modulo 3 with inverse x+2 modulo 3: e(e(0))=2, so this equivalence is not an involution.
